title: The devcontainer and `statespace doctor`
objective: Open the devcontainer, run `statespace doctor` to green, and read the environment block a receipt records.

segments.title: One pinned environment, and its size

blocks.md:
The devcontainer pins the Lean toolchain {{run:RUN-lean-ledger}}, the TLA+ tools by SHA-256 with a Java runtime {{run:RUN-tlc-jars}}, PostgreSQL {{run:RUN-pg-anomalies}}, Z3 {{run:RUN-z3-starter}}, cvc5 and the Rust crates, with their binaries recorded in {{run:RUN-scaffold}}. Each tool is met first in the tab, and the container is for the labs.

Check the sizes before you start. The Lean toolchain unpacks to 3.0G {{run:RUN-lean-toolchain}}. The course uses no Mathlib, and a Mathlib project's packages take 7.3G {{run:RUN-lean-mathlib}}. A Codespaces prebuild is the zero-install route.

`statespace doctor` checks the pins and the sandbox and prints a receipt-ready environment block {{run:RUN-doctor-devcontainer}}. Green means the environment matches the pins. It checks no proof, and a failed sandbox does not turn it red: that is recorded, never required.

Lean builds run in a bubblewrap sandbox on Linux only, and the receipt records it as on, off or failed, never as required. The threat is self-deception, not attack. Without bubblewrap the comparator exits with code 2. Under default Docker bubblewrap cannot start, and the comparator exits with code 1, the code of a rejection {{run:RUN-lean-bwrap-docker}}. A checker killed for memory exits like a rejection too {{run:RUN-bwrap-lanes}}. With the sandbox disabled, `lake check` prints a warning that the run is not trustworthy {{run:RUN-lean-axioms}}.

So receipts parse verdict lines and never trust an exit code alone. A failed sandbox is told from a rejection by a `bwrap:` line, and the first `bwrap:` line names the cause. `statespace doctor` prints the matching hint {{run:RUN-bwrap-lanes}}:

| What the first line says | What it means | What changes it |
|---|---|---|
| it cannot create a new namespace | the container's seccomp profile blocks namespace flags, as Docker's default profile does, or the host forbids unprivileged user namespaces | the devcontainer's opt-in sandbox profile; on a host, allow unprivileged user namespaces |
| it cannot mount proc | the container masks `/proc` paths | `systempaths=unconfined` |
| it cannot create `/run/user` on a read-only file system | the image has no `/run/user` | create the directory in the image |
| `pivot_root` is not permitted | seccomp blocks `pivot_root`, which Docker's default profile does even with extra capabilities | allow it, as the opt-in profile does |
| `unshare`, `mount` or `umount2` is not permitted | seccomp blocks that call | allow them |
| a uid map or loopback setup is denied | Ubuntu 24.04's AppArmor restriction on unprivileged user namespaces | on the host, the sysctl or an AppArmor profile for the binary |
| `mount` is denied on the root | Docker's AppArmor profile denies it | `apparmor=unconfined` in the container |
| the tool says it needs bubblewrap and could not find it | bubblewrap is not installed or not on `PATH` | install it |

macOS and Windows learners use the devcontainer. The lab zip's agent kit travels with it, and its hook blocks agent edits to `TODO(you)` bodies, challenge files, claims and receipts.

notes: Question: what do the sandbox and --paranoid mode do on CI runners, Docker Desktop and Codespaces, how long does --paranoid take on the LAB-2 challenge pack, and how does statespace check tell a sandbox failure from a rejection? The decision record is docs/spikes/W0-S06.md.

The real lanes could not be run on this machine. configs[] holds local emulations, each labeled; lanes{} lists, for each lane, what stands in for it, what was not tested and the owner action that completes it.

The pack is the whole-lab configuration of curriculum/S02-proof.md section 3. Its statements are copied verbatim from the S02 spec (pack/lab2/challenge/Challenge.lean, public). Its three solution files, Solution.lean (proofs of the seven whole-lab theorems), broken/Broken.lean and fixed/Fixed.lean, are complete proofs and are not published: they are reference solutions, which stay in a private place (spine section 11.1). inputs[] lists them by SHA-256 with the role "private fixture, not published", as it lists the eight rejected solutions that mutate.mjs makes from Solution.lean; private-fixtures.json holds the same values. Broken and Fixed import Solution, because lake check loads every default target into one environment and fails with "environment already contains" when two of them define the same name.

The recorded configurations ran while the three files and eight rejected solutions were still inside the pack folder: each docker-run.argv mounts scripts/spikes/W0-S06/pack at /pack and names /pack/lab2 and /pack/variants. They have since been moved out of the public tree. The harness now takes the three from --solutions DIR (mounted at /solutions) and has mutate.mjs make the rejected solutions from Solution.lean (mounted at /variants); mutate.mjs --solutions DIR --verify shows that the files the harness is given have the SHA-256 values in inputs[] and that the eight it makes are byte for byte the ones that ran. The files were last modified at 2026-10-24T12:52:41Z, before the first configuration started (2026-10-24T13:41:34Z), and the hashes in inputs[] are theirs: runs/RUN-bwrap-lanes/private-fixtures-provenance.txt lists each file's hash and modification time, read from the copies kept outside the repository, and the result of comparing the eight rejected solutions that mutate.mjs makes with the files that ran. The probe wrote no fixtures.sha256 then; a configuration recorded with the present harness carries one (hashes only), and open[] names any that used other files.

A side trial, scripts/spikes/W0-S06/collision-trial.sh, is kept in runs/RUN-bwrap-lanes/trial-module-collision/: two libraries whose root modules are both named SelfTransfer, as the S02 layout sketch has. Lake built one SelfTransfer.olean, from the first library, never built the second, and lake build and lake check both exited 0.
Every step records the 1-, 5- and 15-minute load average at its start. This is a shared host: its timings were taken under whatever load other jobs put on it, and they are not promises.

inputs[] holds the hashes of the harness files as they were when this record was assembled. run-matrix.sh gained the container tagging (--cidfile) and the call to collect-oom.mjs after the first pass of the matrix had run, so the local configurations other than local-narrow-std carry no kernel-oom.txt, and local-narrow-std was recorded a second time, alone, for that reason (see its note.txt); the Docker configurations on the virtual machine, recorded later, carry a kernel-oom.txt that says whether the guest could read its kernel log.

classify.mjs is the reference rule. expectations.mjs holds what each step was built to show, written from how the step is constructed and from exploratory runs made before this recorded run, and not from the classifier's output.

notes: The image is a local build, made by the devcontainer CLI from bench/image/Dockerfile as statespace_devcontainer-bench and tagged statespace-bench:w0t05 here. Its digest is the image manifest's (with Docker's containerd image store and no attestation, the image ID); a registry digest exists only once CI pushes the image, and the nightly and monthly lanes read it from the repository variable BENCH_IMAGE (W0-T04). The devcontainer was brought up with STATESPACE_BENCH_IMAGE set to statespace-bench@sha256:b161b2a1d80430f47efa4f326db727f5c44e7a946ecd4aad4f13616b58a02e09, so the doctor report and its receipt block carry that digest. The cold build's manifest digest was sha256:8bf2a44a100313e0d87b7939ddcf0158e95c32b2efd1d858355946049142a94e, and the cached build's, the digest of record, is sha256:b161b2a1d80430f47efa4f326db727f5c44e7a946ecd4aad4f13616b58a02e09: they hold the same 21 layers and differ in the image config (checks cold-and-cached-builds-have-the-same-layers and devcontainer-up-reproduces-the-image-digest). The cause was not isolated in this run; in a scratch trial that is not recorded here, an image built with the argument BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1, which the devcontainer CLI passes, carried a moby.buildkit.cache.v0 entry in its config, and a cold and a cached build of a two-line Dockerfile differed in their IDs. A build in another place or at another time will have other layers, because they hold file times and the Ubuntu packages of the day.

The devcontainer CLI does not run the image byte for byte: it adds the labels of devcontainer.json to the built image (already part of statespace-bench@sha256:b161b2a1d80430f47efa4f326db727f5c44e7a946ecd4aad4f13616b58a02e09) and, because this host's user and the image's user differ in group id, one layer that sets the user ids. The container's image has 22 layers, and its first 21 are the built image's (check devcontainer-runs-the-built-layers).

The recorded build ran without the layer cache (devcontainer build --no-cache), in a clean copy of the working tree (2678 files: the tracked files and the untracked files that .gitignore lets through), so every download was checked against its pinned SHA-256 again and the last step of the Dockerfile, statespace doctor, ran on the fresh image. With the cache warm the same build takes seconds.

Sizes, each as its command reports it: docker image inspect Size 1663129890 bytes; docker images 7.63GB; du of the unpacked root file system 5799502321 bytes (a root-owned container reading its own tree); the sum of the layer sizes in docker history 5969502208 bytes. Which of them is a download size was not measured: no registry was involved.

Where the TLC jars ship: in the image at /opt/tla2tools/, copied by the Dockerfile from bench/image/tla2tools/ in the repository and checked against the SHA-256 values of RUN-tlc-jars. They are vendored because the v1.8.0 release is re-published under its tag: tla2tools-release-asset.json is the asset as the GitHub API listed it when this run was recorded, and it is not the jar the course ran (its SHA-256 differs from the pinned one).

The memory cap is applied with docker update after devcontainer up --skip-post-create and before devcontainer run-user-commands, so the postCreateCommand (statespace doctor) and every later command ran under the 6 GiB cap, on the devcontainer.json as shipped. The opt-in run uses a copy of devcontainer.json in which the one line named by its comment lists docker-compose.sandbox.yml too, with absolute paths.

The default devcontainer reports the sandbox as failed with the line W0-S06 recorded for default Docker, and the run is still green: the sandbox is recorded and never required. The opt-in profile starts it on this host, which has no AppArmor (RUN-bwrap-lanes). On an Ubuntu 24.04 host the profile is not enough; Codespaces and Docker Desktop were not run.

The pins of the Rust toolchain's binaries, of Java and of the Z3 wheel's files were first hashed by this run; every other hash is one that an earlier run recorded (the Lean toolchain's eight binaries by RUN-bwrap-lanes, the jars by RUN-tlc-jars, cvc5 and uv by RUN-scaffold, Soufflé by RUN-souffle-version).

Ubuntu packages (bubblewrap, git, build-essential, libclang-dev, openssh-client, unzip, less, and what Soufflé's package depends on) come from the Ubuntu 24.04 archive of the day and are not pinned by version; the image digest is what pins them.

Only linux/amd64 was built and run. The Dockerfile and the compose file force that platform, because every hash is the x86_64 build's; on Apple silicon Docker Desktop would run the image under emulation, which was not measured (W0-S06 owner action 3).
The build-time check leaves PostgreSQL out (a service container) and records the sandbox as off by choice, because the sandbox cannot start during a build.
The devcontainer CLI is run through npx at the version in the argv; its npm integrity value is in values.devcontainer_cli.

RUN-pg-anomalies.title: PostgreSQL 18.6: the isolation table of RESULTS.md (conditional UPDATE, read-modify-write, write skew, NULL, 22003)
verdict_lines: | Two concurrent `UPDATE acct SET bal = bal - 80 WHERE id=1 AND bal >= 80` from bal=100 | READ COMMITTED | both statements "ok"; second re-evaluates WHERE on the new row version (EvalPlanQual), updates 0 rows; final bal **20** — **no lost update** |
| App-level read-modify-write: both `SELECT bal` (100), both `UPDATE … SET bal = <read>-80` | READ COMMITTED | final bal **20**, but **160 spent from 100** — lost update / double spend |
| Same read-modify-write | REPEATABLE READ | second writer: **SerializationFailure, SQLSTATE 40001**; final 20 |
| Write skew: invariant sum(team) ≥ 0, each txn checks sum (200) then withdraws 150 from a *different* account | REPEATABLE READ | **both commit; team total −100** |
| Same write skew | SERIALIZABLE | t1 commits, t2 **40001**; total 50 |
| `UPDATE … SET bal = bal - 10 WHERE bal >= 10` over rows {NULL, 50} | — | only the non-NULL row updated; the NULL row is **silently skipped** |
| `9223372036854775807::bigint + 1` | — | **error 22003 "bigint out of range"** — Postgres raises, it does not wrap |
notes: Imported by W0-S11 from research/spikes/pg_anomalies.py; RESULTS.md (spine section 9.5). The verdict lines are copied verbatim from the outputs listed here; every file is hashed as it is on disk now.

RUN-scaffold.title: The scaffold's pinned stack: the site, the Bench's Python and Rust sides, and the cvc5 Bench binary
RUN-scaffold.version: react 19.3.1, react-router 7.18.4, vite 7.3.7, typescript 5.9.3, playwright 1.63.0, axe-core 4.14.0

budget.network: downloads from npm, PyPI, crates.io, apt, rustup and GitHub releases; the browser and cvc5 containers run with the network off

values.cvc5_build: compiled as a unrestricted build with GCC version 11.4.0 on Oct  8 2026 01:24:07

notes: RUN-scaffold pins several tools at once, so the top-level engine names the record and the top-level version is the site stack; each configuration carries its own engine, version, binary_sha256 (where a binary ran), argv, inputs, budget, exit code and verdict lines. Named values (values.*) are what copy cites with {{run:RUN-scaffold#values.<name>}}.

Where a configuration ran: npm, node, uv and cargo ran on the host (Linux x86_64, Node 22). The browser configurations ran in the Playwright image of the same version as @playwright/test, which carries Node 24, so the site and instruments suites ran on Node 24 there; the unit tests and the build ran on Node 22 on the host. The Rust crate check, the wasm build and cvc5 ran in ubuntu:24.04; PostgreSQL ran in postgres:18, reached on a loopback port.

Not executed here: the arm64 build of cvc5 (hashed only; no arm64 emulation on this host) and everything on macOS, Windows or Apple silicon. Soufflé ships no arm64 package at all (RUN-souffle-version).

The PostgreSQL entry pins the service image by digest: postgres:18 is a moving tag, and the digest is what the devcontainer compose file must use. It reports PostgreSQL 18.6, the pin of labs/TOOLS.md.

The Rust crates are the candidates labs/TOOLS.md read from the crates.io API on 2026-10-23, pinned with `=` and resolved into the committed Cargo.lock. On Ubuntu 24.04 `cargo check --locked` passes with build-essential and libclang-dev installed (plus curl and ca-certificates, which only rustup needs): pg_query compiles libpg_query with the C compiler and generates its bindings with libclang. bench-rust-host-without-libclang records the same check stopping at pg_query on a host with no libclang, so the Bench image must carry libclang-dev (W0-T05). The recorded run installs nothing else: no clang binary, no protoc, no pkg-config.

The cvc5 Bench binary is the non-GPL static build, so its version string reads 1.4.2 and carries no -modified suffix, unlike the pip wheel of RUN-cvc5-alethe. The two are different builds of the same release: a receipt records the string verbatim.

kit-wasm-roundtrip is the one check that the vendored ABI pair (the host code and the kit crate) still agrees: a module built by the pinned toolchain against the vendored kit, driven by the vendored host code, unedited.

The browser smoke tests are the scaffold's own: a meta CSP present and nothing blocked, no request to another origin, no console error, axe with no violation at 360, 320 and 1280 px, no sideways scroll. GATE-bundle and GATE-a11y proper are built on the shell (W1).
Re-record this run after any change to package.json, a workspace manifest or package-lock.json: the npm-lock configuration lists their SHA-256 values as inputs, and GATE-runs compares them.
duration_s on the record is the sum of the configurations; informational outputs (summaries with durations) are compared on verdict_lines when the run is re-recorded.
